jurisdictions_with_solid_material: Ontario provincial (Ministry of Finance budget cycle, Public Accounts)
City of Toronto (budget, consolidated financial statements, tax levy by-law)
City of Ottawa (budget, annual financial report / consolidated statements)
confirmation.notes: Ontario municipal-finance vocabulary uses 'Financial Information Return (FIR)' for the standardized municipal return (existing on-municipal-fir), 'Tax Levy By-law' for the annual property-tax rate setting instrument (Toronto example found), and 'Annual Financial Report' / 'Consolidated Financial Statements' prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards. No forced Alberta-style labels. MPAC assessments are the explicit input to municipal tax calculations and to OMPF Assessment Equalization. Municipal audited statements are the basis for FIR submissions. Coverage stopped when primary sources ceased yielding new verifiable nodes/edges; Toronto and Ottawa are the priority municipalities requested and both publish the core set.

proposed_reports.title: Ontario Budget
proposed_reports.description: Annual provincial budget document presenting the government's economic outlook, fiscal plan, revenue and expense projections, borrowing program, and policy measures. Includes the multi-year path to balance, net debt-to-GDP projections, and detailed fiscal tables. Most recent: 2026 Ontario Budget: A Plan to Protect Ontario (tabled March 2026).
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: Annual (typically spring); supplemented by Fall Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review and quarterly finances updates

proposed_reports.title: Ontario Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review (Fall Statement)
proposed_reports.description: Mid-year update to the economic and fiscal outlook, revising GDP, revenue, expense and deficit projections relative to the spring Budget. Contains updated medium-term fiscal plan and economic assumptions. Example: 2025 Ontario Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review.

proposed_reports.title: Public Accounts of Ontario
proposed_reports.publisher: Treasury Board Secretariat / Ontario Ministry of Finance (audited by Auditor General of Ontario)
proposed_reports.description: Annual audited consolidated financial statements of the Province of Ontario for the fiscal year ended 31 March, including the Annual Report, Consolidated Financial Statements, Ministry Statements and Schedules, and Detailed Schedules of Payments. Prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards and compared against the Budget plan.

proposed_reports.title: City of Toronto Operating and Capital Budget
proposed_reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and multi-year capital budget and plan adopted by City Council (Mayor's proposed budget under City of Toronto Act). Includes property-tax levy requirements, service-area allocations, and 10-year capital plan. Most recent: 2026 Operating Budget ($18.9 billion) and 2026–2035 Capital Budget and Plan ($63.1 billion).

proposed_reports.title: City of Toronto Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Financial Report
proposed_reports.publisher: City of Toronto (Finance & Treasury; audited by external auditor)
proposed_reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements (including sinking funds and trust funds) prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB). Accompanied by the Annual Financial Report providing narrative and statistical context. Most recent complete: 2024 statements approved 2025; 2025 draft statements available 2026.

proposed_reports.title: City of Toronto Tax Levy By-law
proposed_reports.description: Annual by-law enacted under the City of Toronto Act setting the municipal tax ratios, general local municipal levy, additional rates for budgetary increase and City Building Fund, and resulting tax rates by property class. Generates the property-tax revenue authorized by the adopted budget. Example: By-law 133-2026 (Tax Levy By-law for 2026).

proposed_reports.title: City of Ottawa Operating and Capital Budget
proposed_reports.description: Annual tax- and rate-supported operating budget and capital budget adopted by Council under the Municipal Act. Must be balanced. Includes property-tax levy, transit levy, water/sewer rates, and multi-year capital authority. Example: 2025 Adopted Budget; 2026 draft presented late 2025.

proposed_reports.title: City of Ottawa Consolidated Financial Statements / Annual Report
proposed_reports.publisher: City of Ottawa (Finance and Corporate Services; audited by external auditor)
proposed_reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAB) as required by the Municipal Act, accompanied by the Annual Report containing financial statement discussion and analysis and statistical schedules. Most recent: 2024 Annual Report (released 2025); 2025 statements presented 2026.

dependencies.basis: Municipal tax rates are applied to the current-year phased-in property assessment values determined by MPAC to calculate individual property tax bills and to raise the total municipal levy authorized by the budget.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Your property tax bill is calculated by multiplying the current year phased-in property assessment value, as determined by the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC), by Council approved City Tax Rate(s) with the City Building Fund Levy and the Education Tax Rate, as set by the Government of Ontario.

dependencies.basis: The Tax Levy By-law sets the exact tax rates and ratios required to generate the municipal tax levy amount decided upon in the adopted operating budget.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Whereas subsection 228(1) of the City of Toronto Act, 2006... provides for the City in each year to adopt a budget including estimates of all sums required... and Whereas section 277 of the Act provides that the general local municipality levy is the amount the City decides to raise in its budget for the year...

dependencies.basis: City of Toronto consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board.
dependencies.evidence_quote: All City financial statements are prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board of the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada.

dependencies.basis: City of Ottawa consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board as required by the Ontario Municipal Act.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The City of Ottawa’s 2024 Annual Report contains the audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board [‘PSAB’] of the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada [“CPA Canada”], as required by the Ontario Municipal Act.

dependencies.basis: The provincial Financial Information Return is compiled from municipal submissions that are based on each municipality’s audited financial statements; the Ministry reviews submitted FIRs against the audited statements for consistency.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Through the FIR template... the Ministry collects data on municipal financial position and activities, such as assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, over the course of the previous fiscal year (based on the audited financial statements)... Once submitted, a municipality’s FIR is reviewed and compared with the audited financial statements to ensure consistency.

dependencies.basis: OMPF Assessment Equalization Grant and other components use weighted assessment per household and household counts derived from the MPAC returned assessment roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Weighted Assessment | 2024 Returned Roll and 2025 starting tax ratios | Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) and municipal tax rate bylaws ... Number of Households | 2024 | MPAC Returned Roll

dependencies.basis: Certain OMPF data inputs (e.g., PIL weighted assessment) are drawn from municipal Financial Information Returns.
dependencies.evidence_quote: PIL Weighted Assessment | 2022 or 2023 | Municipal FIR

dependencies.basis: OMPF uses Statistics Canada census-derived indicators including median household income, rural and small community measure, percent of population above low-income threshold, and ratio of working-age to dependent population.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Median Household Income | 2021 | Statistics Canada ... Rural and Small Community Measure | 2021 | Statistics Canada ... Per Cent of Population Above Low-Income Threshold | 2021 | Statistics Canada ... Ratio of Working Age to Dependent Population | 2021 | Statistics Canada

dependencies.basis: The Consolidated Financial Statements of the Province are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards and are audited by the Auditor General of Ontario.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Public Accounts are prepared by the Treasury Board Secretariat and the Ontario government’s consolidated financial statements are independently audited by the Auditor General every year.

dependencies.basis: The Budget presents a forward-looking fiscal plan that is subsequently compared against actual results reported in the Public Accounts; the Public Accounts explicitly compare performance to the Budget plan.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Public Accounts presents the government’s financial statements and gives a picture of how finances were managed over the last fiscal year... It compares the Ontario government’s financial performance with the goals outlined in the budget.

dependencies.basis: Budget communications and tax-impact illustrations use MPAC average current-value assessment figures for the typical Toronto home when quantifying the dollar effect of proposed tax-rate increases.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In total, the combined residential property tax increase and City Building Fund levy represent an increase of 2.2 per cent, or $91.53 per year ($7.63 per month), based on the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation’s average current value assessment of a Toronto home ($692,140).

dependencies.basis: Property-tax calculations and budget illustrations rely on assessed values determined by MPAC; tax policy pages state that one-quarter of a residential bill is education tax set by the Province while the municipal portion is based on local assessment.
dependencies.evidence_quote: One-quarter of a residential property tax bill is effectively set or mandated by the Province. Education taxes are set by the Province and collected by the City.

dependencies.basis: Provincial budgets incorporate federal health and social transfers as major revenue sources within the overall fiscal plan; the Budget documents and fiscal tables treat CHT/CST as part of the revenue outlook that underpins program expense decisions.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Revenues in 2025–26 are projected to be $226.6 billion... Total revenue is projected to increase from $226.2 billion in 2024–25 to $254.1 billion in 2028–29.

dependencies.basis: The Annual Financial Report and consolidated statements present actual results against the Council-approved budget and discuss budget-to-actual variances for operating and capital activities.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The budget includes details of the planned operating and capital activities, as well as proposed property tax rate and user fee changes for the year. ... Summary of the 2024 Council approved budget

dependencies.basis: The consolidated financial statements include a reconciliation of the Council-approved modified-accrual budget to the full-accrual PSAB presentation and report actuals against budget figures.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Budget data presented in these consolidated financial statements is based upon the 2024 operating and capital budgets approved by Council on December 6, 2023. Council-approved budgets are prepared on a modified accrual basis, which differs from budget amounts reported on the consolidated statement of operations and accumulated surplus, which are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards.
